Tracking Data

Tracking data contained in this report is largely drawn from the 1992 "Health of the Planet" survey conducted by the Gallup International Institute.

Geographical Region

The countries which are studied in this report have been grouped into four categories of economic development. Industrialized countries consist of those countries in Western Europe, North America, Oceania, as well as Japan, which exhibit very high levels of affluence and economic development. Transitional economies consist of Eastern European countries in the former Soviet bloc which are in transition from having centrally planned economies, to having more market driven economies. Emerging countries such as Mexico, Chile, China and Korea are formerly developing countries which are now displaying rapid economic growth and industrialization. Developing countries, such as India, Peru, and Nigeria are at lower stages of economic development with large proportions of their populations living at a subsistence level.

Figures and Charts

All figures ad charts in this report are expressed in percentages. Total percentages may not add up because of rounding. More detailed tabular results for each question are available to our subscribers on a request basis.

Environics International Environmental Monitor, 1997 is the first commercially available monitor of global environmental attitudes since the 1992 Earth Summit in Rio de Janeiro. One of the objectives was to explore changes in public perceptions over the five-year period since 1992; a period in which environmental concerns have been widely perceived by elites in many countries to be declining in the face of pressing economic concerns.

This report is based on the results of in-home or telephone surveys with representative samples of at least 1,000 citizens in 24 countries on all continents and at varying stages of development (which together represent over 60 percent of the population of the world). A total of 32 questions were posed dealing with such topics as overall environmental perceptions and concerns. Research was conducted by respected social research institutes in each country between December 9, 1996 and April 30, 1997.
